context.objective: Document how we carry out Investor Onboarding, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It starts when a prospective investor subscribes at an initial or subsequent close, or the client tells us an investor is coming in. Let me walk through the whole thing. First, as the investor services onboarding preparer, I open the onboarding checklist and log, record the fund, investor legal name, expected commitment and target close date, and assign myself and the investor services team lead as reviewer. Second, I build the required document list for that investor type and jurisdiction and send one consolidated request list to the authorized party. Third, as documents arrive through Box or PassThru, I save them in the controlled workspace and log the received date and version. Fourth, I review the subscription agreement, commitment, side letter and the W-9 or W-8 tax form for completeness. If documents are incomplete or inconsistent, I issue a consolidated deficiency list and the one-week target clock pauses until the complete set is received. Fifth, I submit the screening package to the AML and KYC role, and they give approval, rejection or conditions. If it is not cleared, we do not accept capital and we do not close onboarding. Sixth, treasury validates new wire instructions by a call back to an independently verified contact. If the callback fails or details change, the instructions are not used and the verification is repeated. Seventh, I send a status package to the client and the client gives written admission approval. If the approval is conditional, I track every condition and it stays open until resolved or waived. Eighth, I create the investor in the CRM, set include in portal to yes, create the investor and commitment in the accounting system, and compare both to the source documents field by field. If they conflict, I correct against the approved source. Ninth, I provision the contacts in the investor portal and test access. If the sync or access fails, we hold the first notice and escalate to the team lead and system support. Tenth, if it is a subsequent close investor, I send commitment, close date and side letter data to the equalization team. I give the static data to the fund team and confirm the investor is in the correct capital call population. Finally, the team lead does the completion review, I send completion confirmation to the client, and I lock the checklist and package and record the actual completion date.
What guides how you determine the required documents for each investor type and jurisdiction?

Honestly, the exact document matrix by investor type and jurisdiction is not confirmed, so I do not know of an approved one. I list the subscription, side letter, tax, AML and KYC, beneficial owner, wire, contact and commitment items. Check the scope against the AML requirements and the client and legal requirements, and anything uncertain I route to the AML role, the client, or the legal advisor. I do not guess.
What does the AML and KYC role use to reach an approval, rejection or conditional decision?

The detailed screening method belongs to a separate AML process, so I do not know it in detail. What I know is they review identity, beneficial ownership, sanctions, politically exposed persons, adverse media, and risk. Using the screening package I submit, I track missing ownership or risk records, false positives get resolved through the AML and client channels, and I record the clearance status and date in the onboarding checklist, which system they use is not confirmed.
What does the team lead check in the completion review?

Normal frequency, who receives or detects the initiating event, and any fixed deadline or date obligation are not established.

At the end, the team lead performs a completion review; the preparer sends completion confirmation to the client, then locks the checklist and package and records the actual completion date.
The specific criteria the team lead checks in the completion review, and whether any downstream posting or reconciliation is required for completion, are not established.

The participant describes performing as the investor services onboarding preparer; the investor services team lead is assigned as reviewer and performs the completion review.
The role accountable for the overall onboarding result, distinct from the preparer and reviewer, is not identified.

If documents are incomplete or inconsistent, the preparer issues a consolidated deficiency list; the one-week target clock pauses until the complete set is received.
The preparer submits a screening package to the AML and KYC role, which gives approval, rejection or conditions. If screening is not cleared, capital is not accepted and onboarding does not close.
